transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, could you tell me what brings you in today?

I keep getting these awful doubts that I’ve missed something important. Like a number on the mortgage payment, something in a client proof, or whether I really latched the door. Even when I know I checked, the thought comes right back—what if that’s the mistake that costs me everything?

When these doubts come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to try to ease them—like going back to check the lock, re-reading the numbers, or asking someone else to confirm things are okay?

Yes. I reopen the files and reread emails over and over, and I check the online payment confirmation repeatedly. Sometimes I say the figures silently in my head until they feel settled. A simple invoice or logo revision can end up taking hours that I can’t bill for.
Between the intrusive doubts themselves and the checking or repeating behaviors you do afterward, which one feels like the bigger problem or takes up more of your time and distress?

The checking, definitely. I can lose hours reopening files, rereading emails, checking the payment confirmation again and again. Sometimes I repeat the figures silently until they feel settled. It turns a simple invoice or logo revision into work I can’t bill for.
How long have you been experiencing these doubts and the checking behaviors—days, weeks, or longer?
I’m not really sure how long it’s been going on. I know it isn’t just a few days, but I can’t pin down when it started.
When you do the checking or repeating—like rereading the emails or confirming the payment—does it actually bring you some relief or a sense of settling, even if only temporarily?
Yes, for a little while. If I reopen the file or check the payment confirmation again, it feels more settled—but then I start doubting it again and go back to it.
Would you say these checking and repeating behaviors have been happening on most days for at least the past two weeks, or has it been more on-and-off than that?
It’s been happening most days, yes. I’ll reopen the files, reread emails, check the payment confirmation—sometimes repeat the figures in my head—and it can eat up hours.
Aside from the checking, how distressing or time-consuming are the doubts and intrusive thoughts themselves, on their own?

They’re pretty distressing on their own. The thought just barges in that I missed something important—a mortgage number, something in a client proof, even whether a door is latched—and then it becomes, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” Even before I check, I can get stuck thinking about it for a long time.
Roughly how much time each day would you say is spent just being stuck on the doubting thoughts themselves, before or apart from any checking you do?

A couple of hours, probably, on a bad day. I can just sit there turning over whether I missed a number or a clause, or whether something wasn’t properly latched, even though I know I already checked. The thought is always, what if this is the one mistake that costs me everything?
